transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Time: 16:00 PST (55 minutes)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Julian (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood CSM), Claire (Galileo Head of Partnerships), Samir (Galileo Sales Lead), Priya (Galileo Solutions Architect), Liam (Galileo CISO)

Summary: short calibration between partner and Redwood on co-selling approach, velocity expectations for pilot, and risk controls. Key asks: performance benchmarks for Dedicated, VPC/KMS constraints, and pricing tiers for burst vs committed capacity.

Topics: partner GTM alignment, pilot success metrics, deployment model tradeoffs (Dedicated vs Private), security/compliance clarification, timeline for pilot and decision.

Action items (from the call): see metadata list.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll keep this tight — 45 to 55 minutes. Quick intros — Julian and Noah from our side. Julian's going to cover perf and deployment tradeoffs, Noah will cover the onboarding and CS touchpoints. Claire, Samir — can you do a 30-second context?
[00:18] Claire: Yeah hi, Claire here — head of partnerships at Galileo. We're exploring a joint go-to-market where we embed Redwood powered features into a verticalized offering. We're trying to understand speed to revenue and risk profile.
[00:34] Samir: And I'm Samir, leading the sales side. Timeline: we'd like to run a pilot in January and then a commercial rollout in Q2, assuming no major security roadblocks.
[00:46] Julian: cool — and Priya?
[00:48] Priya: Priya, I'm the solutions architect. Main technical constraints: need to know latency percentiles at 95/99, ability to pin model versions, and clear KMS integration. Also we'll likely want a VPC peering for the pilot.
[01:05] Liam: Liam, CISO — quick note: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, audit logs for all requests and encryption-in-transit and at-rest assurances. Data residency could be EMEA-only for some customers.
[01:18] Maya: Great context — thanks. I'll hand to Julian to walk through the Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for this use case.
[01:24] Julian: Alright, high level: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC / on-prem). For a partner co-sell pilot that needs predictable latency and some data isolation, Dedicated is usually the sweet spot — predictable throughput and can be scoped with burst capacity for demand spikes. Private is recommended when customers require on-prem or strict network isolation.
[01:48] Claire: When you say Dedicated — is customer data leaving our network? How does the VPC/peering work? We need to understand exposure for enterprise customers.
[02:00] Julian: Dedicated runs in Redwood-managed infra but we offer private networking modes — VPC peering (or PrivateLink in cloud) and we support customer-provided KMS. So logs and payloads are encrypted; we can limit egress regions. There's a slight nuance: Dedicated by default has more ops flexibility and quicker onboarding than full private.
[02:26] Priya: fine — curious about latency. Our workload is chat + reranking, typical inference is a 1k token median but 99th can get spiky. What does the 95/99 look like for your Dedicated pools?
[02:40] Julian: We saw 95th ~ 80-120 ms for gpt-family-like models on NVidia H100 pools under normal batching for short prompts; 99th can be 250-400ms depending on KV cache hit rates and the sequence length. Benchmarking with your real payload is the only way to be precise. Also batching and prefix caching impact cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:05] Samir: That's promising but we need guarantees. Can you put a latency SLO into the pilot contract or at least an SLA for Dedicated?
[03:12] Maya: For Dedicated we have latency targets baked into the SLA depending on config; we can commit to latency envelopes and rollback to a smaller model or fallback in overload scenarios. We'll surface specific SLA terms in the partner offer.
[03:24] Liam: SLA's nice, but auditability is critical. We need request-level logs for compliance and proof of data residency. Is there an audit log export we can pipe into our SIEM?
[03:36] Noah: Yep — we can export logs, and Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns. For compliance we offer audit-export (S3 or secure push) and integrations with common SIEMs. The trick is retention windows — we can extend for an enterprise add-on.
[03:58] Claire: pricing — we want to understand partner split and the economics for our joint offering. Will there be partner discounts for volume or co-sell?
[04:08] Maya: Yes — we have partner pricing tiers that include co-sell margins. For pilots we usually offer promotional credits and a partner rebate on committed capacity. I will follow up with a tailored pricing scenario that shows burst vs committed economics.
[04:24] Priya: On the technical side again — model version pinning. We can't have model drift across customers. Can we pin a model and ensure rollouts are controlled?
[04:33] Julian: Absolutely — the deployment abstraction supports model versioning and can do canary rollouts or A/B tests. You can pin per-route or per-customer. We also do quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets, which helps detect regressions after model upgrades.
[04:50] Samir: Competitors question — we've been evaluating Anthropic and Vertex. How do you compare on latency/cost?
[04:58] Julian: Short answer: performance is workload-dependent. Redwood's value prop is cost-aware controls — batching, KV caching, quantization recommendations — and a unified runtime that runs well across Dedicated/Private. For latency we optimize kernel selection and attention optimizations — so in many cases our latencies are competitive; cost often beats the managed cloud endpoints after you tune batching and caching.
[05:20] Liam: About KMS — if we bring our own KMS, are keys ever visible to Redwood ops?
[05:26] Noah: No — with a customer-managed KMS we only see ciphertext; key material stays in your KMS, and we can integrate with major cloud KMS/HSM providers. For fully private on-prem we can do HSM integrations.
[05:40] Claire: Pilot success metrics — Samir and I talked about revenue-touch in 3 months, but what technical metrics should we measure?
[05:50] Maya: Typical pilot metrics: 95/99 latency targets, error rate < 0.5%, token cost per session, and business metrics — conversion lift or time-to-completion for the flow you're instrumenting. We'll work with Priya to make an instrumentation plan.
[06:06] Priya: We'll provide sample traffic and business funnels — mostly chat sessions of 300-1k tokens, plus a reranking job that runs post-session. Expect mixed sequence lengths and some heavy tails.
[06:18] Julian: For the reranking path, we often recommend batching and possibly a cheaper reranker model to reduce token cost; we can propose a two-stage architecture in the design doc.
[06:30] Samir: Operationally — onboarding time? We need to be able to demo something to a strategic customer in late Jan.
[06:38] Maya: Realistic timeline: setup + security review in 2 weeks, pilot config and bench in week 3, pilot start by end of January. We'll prioritize the workstream since it's co-sell.
[06:50] Liam: Security review cadence — we need a contact to run our risk questionnaire and to get the SOC2 report.
[06:57] Maya: I'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts. Noah will be your onboarding contact.
[07:05] Noah: I'll coordinate the security questionnaire and ask for the minimal data flows mapping. Also will set the retention and log export options.
[07:15] Claire: Are there any known limitations — like model architecture constraints or model size limits for Dedicated?
[07:23] Julian: We support a wide catalog; the main limit is GPU memory for very large context/large models. For extremely long contexts we use KV cache optimizations and may recommend model quantization or model-splitting strategies. Sometimes the transcript may show 'k v cache' in logs, apologies for auto transcription there.
[07:44] Priya: Ok — one more question: who owns the customer-facing billing and contract? If we co-sell, do you invoice Galileo or the end-customer?
[07:55] Maya: We do both models. For pure referral/reseller we invoice Galileo and provide partner margin. For direct co-sell we can set up revenue share and invoice the end-customer while providing Galileo with partner credits. We'll include those options in the pricing scenario.
[08:12] Samir: Good. On the pilot we'll need a tight escalation path. Can we get a single point of contact for incidents?
[08:20] Noah: Yes — we'll assign a technical CSM and provide an on-call contact during ramp. For Dedicated we usually provide a higher-touch support SLA.
[08:32] Claire: This is helpful — what do you need from us today to get moving?
[08:36] Maya: From a Redwood POV: sample payloads, desired SLOs, list of pilot stakeholders (decision maker + technical owner), and confirmation on whether you need DPA/KMS specifics up front.
[08:50] Priya: We'll send sample payloads and the SLO doc by Friday 2026-12-13.
[08:57] Liam: We'll share the acceptable residency constraints and KMS specs by 2026-12-15.
[09:04] Claire: We'll confirm the pilot stakeholders by Monday 2026-12-13.
[09:10] Maya: Great — next steps recap: I'll send partner co-sell one-pager and tailored pricing; Julian will run a targeted latency perf run with your payload once Priya uploads it; Noah will kick off security questionnaire and SOC2 exchange. We'll plan a technical pilot kickoff the week of Jan 5.
[09:30] Samir: Sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood's side that we should be aware of?
[09:36] Julian: Nothing major — just need the payload and SLOs to make perf numbers meaningful. Also if you have strict EMEA-only residency we might push to Private depending on the customer's legal needs, but we can often meet residency with dedicated region controls.
[09:52] Maya: Alright — thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with artifacts and calendar invites.
[09:58] Claire: Thanks, everyone.
[10:00] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mistranscribed acronyms (e.g., 'k v cache' / 'KV cache'), speaker overlaps and filler words. Where precise legal wording is required (SLA, DPA), refer to formal contracts — this transcript is a sales artifact only.
